title: The Koszul differential squares to zero
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $E$ an $R$-module, $\varphi:E\to R$ an $R$-linear map, and $D:\wedge(E)\to\wedge(E)$ the $R$-linear map of [lem-weil-pbc-koszul-differential] (the unique one with $D(1)=0$ and $D(v\wedge x)=\varphi(v)x-v\wedge D(x)$ for $v\in E$, $x\in\wedge(E)$, where $\wedge(E)$ is the exterior algebra [def-weil-pbc-exterior-algebra]). Then $D\circ D=0$. In particular, writing $d_n:\wedge^n_R(E)\to\wedge^{n-1}_R(E)$ for the restriction of $D$, one has $d_{n-1}\circ d_n=0$ for all $n\ge1$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Definition Tag 0622 (definition-koszul, line 6566): K_bullet(phi) is called a (commutative) differential graded algebra with differential d, which presupposes d o d = 0; Stacks does not write the computation (for the generators: d(d(v wedge x)) = phi(v)d(x) - phi(v)d(x) + v wedge d(d(x)), induction on the degree). Tag verified in tags/tags.

proof.text: For a wedge monomial, the empty case gives $D^2(1)=D(0)=0$. Suppose $D^2(v_2\wedge\cdots\wedge v_n)=0$. Applying the recursion from [lem-weil-pbc-koszul-differential] twice gives $D^2(v_1\wedge x)=D(\varphi(v_1)x-v_1\wedge D(x))=\varphi(v_1)D(x)-D(v_1\wedge D(x))=v_1\wedge D^2(x)$, where $x=v_2\wedge\cdots\wedge v_n$. Thus $D^2(v_1\wedge\cdots\wedge v_n)=0$ by induction on $n$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Definition Tag 0622 and the paragraph after it (definition-koszul, lines 6560-6590); the omitted generator computation is written out here.

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-exterior-algebra], the wedge monomials span each exterior power and their direct sum is $\wedge(E)$. Since $D^2$ is $R$-linear and vanishes on every such monomial by step 1, it vanishes on all of $\wedge(E)$, so $D\circ D=0$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Definition Tag 0622, the description of the exterior algebra and its homogeneous generators immediately preceding and following line 6566.

proof.text: For $n\ge1$, the restriction $d_n$ is $D|_{\wedge^n_R(E)}$ and the restriction $d_{n-1}$ is $D|_{\wedge^{n-1}_R(E)}$ by the degree statement in [lem-weil-pbc-koszul-differential]. Therefore $d_{n-1}\circ d_n$ is the restriction of $D\circ D$ to $\wedge^n_R(E)$, hence is zero by step 2.
